name: Geophysics (MS)

rules.name: Requirements Overview
rules.desc:
Students must complete a minimum of 45 units of coursework. Lecture courses (component LEC) must be taken for a letter grade unless S/NC is the only option offered. Students must maintain a GPA of 3.0 (B) grade point average overall in courses applicable to the degree. Students are encouraged, but not required, to attend the department seminar.
Program Objectives: To enhance the student’s training for professional work in geophysics through completing courses and independent research.
How We Study: Complete at least one course from any of the following 4 areas.

rules.name: Area 1. Computational methods involving data-intensive computing or numerical modeling [grouped below by subject area]
Area 2. Laboratory-scale studies of physical properties and processes
Area 3. Observations of Earth and planets using various forms of measurement (waves and potential fields)
Area 4: Physics-based modeling of Earth processes and materials
What We Study
rules.desc:
“What we study” in geophysics ranges broadly across many areas: atmosphere, climate, cryosphere, energy, freshwater, geomaterials, hazards, oceans, other planets, tectonics/geodynamics/Earth’s interior.
In consultation with their faculty advisor, students must identify and take 1-2 courses, each at least three units, that enhance their understanding of “what they study” or provide breadth and understanding in other areas of “what we study.”
A small subset of the classes from the “How We Study” list (the 4 areas identified there/above) may be used to satisfy the “What We Study” requirement.
Such a class may be used to fulfill either the “How we study” or “What we study” requirement, but not both. These classes are:

• GEOPHYS 230

• GEOPHYS 239

rules.name: Additional courses to reach 45 units (advisor-approved; GEOPHYS 400 may be used)
rules.desc: The remaining units, to reach a total of 45 units, are from courses deemed relevant by the student and advisor to the student’s education in geophysics. GEOPHYS 400 can be used for some or all of these units.

rules.name: Research presentation and report
rules.desc: The student must present their research in a public, oral presentation attended by their advisor and one other Stanford faculty member and submit a written report to their advisor.

rules.name: GPA of 3.0 in courses applicable to the degree

gpa: Students must maintain a GPA of 3.0 (B) grade point average overall in courses applicable to the degree.
grading: Lecture courses (component LEC) must be taken for a letter grade unless S/NC is the only option offered.
reviewNotes: The audit checks the 45 units, GEOPHYS 201, 6 units of GEOPHYS 400, and one course from each of the four How We Study areas, with lecture courses letter graded unless S/NC is the only option. Checked by hand: the 1-2 What We Study courses chosen with your advisor (GEOPHYS 230 or 239 count there or under How We Study, not both), the advisor-approved courses that make up the rest of the 45 units, the research presentation and report, and the 3.0 GPA. The overview's "at least one course from any of the following 4 areas" could also mean one course in all; the audit asks for one per area.
